I read the earlier post about modification indices and how they relate to Wald and Lagrange multiplier tests.

Is there accessible code to to run the Lagrange multiplier method multivariately, instead of univariately? As I understand it, the tests that are run in the modindices() command return univariate tests..

Thanks very much,
Gretel

On 03/29/2016 10:55 AM, Marcos Angelini wrote:
> Hi to all,
>
> I am trying to find literature about the test involved in the function
> modIndices(). Could you provide me some, please?

See:

Sörbom, D. (1989). Model modification. Psychometrika, 54(3), 371-384.

Saris, W. E., Satorra, A., & Sörbom, D. (1987). The detection and
correction of specification errors in structural equation models.
Sociological methodology, 17, 105-129.

Of course, the modification index is simply the univariate Lagrange
multiplier (aka Rao's score) test, for which there is tons of literature.

> On Tuesday, 28 January 2014 18:22:02 UTC+1, Gretel Clarke wrote:
>
> Hi all,
>
> I read the earlier post about modification indices and how they
> relate to Wald and Lagrange multiplier tests.
>
> Is there accessible code to to run the Lagrange multiplier method
> multivariately, instead of univariately? As I understand it, the
> tests that are run in the modindices() command return univariate tests..

While I am here: the answer today is YES: see the lavTestScore() function.

For literature about the 'multivariate' Lagrange multiplier test, see:

Bentler, P. M., & Chou, C. P. (1993). Some new covariance structure
model improvement statistics. Sage Focus Editions, 154, 235-255.

Yves.
